hypothesis: Combine the two independently-successful mechanisms: keep the parent's CTS sink clustering (size=1, diameter=50) and additionally fine-tune it modestly (x2 diameter to 100) so clustered sinks still avoid long clock-detour while reducing buffer/routing pressure — a small coefficient step on the best-known knob rather than a new mechanism.
analysis: The hypothesis did not hold: total score is negative (-0.057) and robustly so (mean-std -0.060), with all three cases valid. The modest diameter x2 step hurt bp-ng45 most (dWNS -12.9%), while bp_fe-ng45 improved slightly (+0.036, dTNS +6.6%) and ariane133-ng45 was mildly negative. Plausible mechanism: doubling diameter over-clusters sinks, adding detour/buffer pressure that outweighs routing savings on the sensitive bp case. Next step: sweep diameter between 50 and 100 (e.g., 60/75) per-case rather than a single global x2, and gate the change to cases where overflow is high.
